name: Place a probability on a 0 to 1 scale
description: Student can place the likelihood of an event on a numerical scale from 0 to 1.
exampleOfSuccess: The student places a fair coin landing heads at 0.5 on the scale.
commonError: Student places certain events below impossible ones, or reverses the scale.
checkpointTask: Give events. Ask the student to place each on a 0 to 1 probability scale.

name: Assign a probability as a fraction
description: Student can assign a probability to an event as a common fraction.
exampleOfSuccess: For rolling a 6 on a dice, the student gives 1/6.
commonError: Student gives the number of outcomes rather than the fraction.
checkpointTask: Pose chance events. Ask the student to assign a probability as a fraction.

name: Express a probability as a percentage or decimal
description: Student can express a probability as a percentage or decimal.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes a 1/2 chance as 50% or 0.5.
checkpointTask: Give probabilities as fractions. Ask the student to write each as a percentage and decimal.

name: Estimate a probability in context
description: Student can use estimation to assign a probability in a given context.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates the chance of rain as about 70% from the forecast.
commonError: Student assigns a probability with no basis in the context.
checkpointTask: Pose contexts. Ask the student to estimate the probability of each.

name: Run a chance simulation
description: Student can run a simulation of a chance experiment using a digital tool.
exampleOfSuccess: The student uses a digital tool to simulate many coin tosses.
commonError: Student runs too few trials, or does not record the results.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to run a chance simulation and record the results.

name: Compare observed and expected results
description: Student can compare observed frequencies with expected results.
exampleOfSuccess: The student compares the simulated heads count with the expected half.
commonError: Student expects the observed results to match the expected exactly.
checkpointTask: After a simulation, ask the student to compare the observed and expected results.

name: Increase the number of trials
description: Student can observe what happens to results as the number of trials increases.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notices the proportion of heads gets closer to half with more trials.
commonError: Student thinks more trials make the results less reliable.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to increase the trials in a simulation and describe what happens.

name: Discuss the effect on variation
description: Student can discuss how increasing trials affects the variation in results.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains that more trials reduce the variation from the expected value.
commonError: Student cannot connect the number of trials to the variation.
checkpointTask: After simulations of different sizes, ask the student to discuss the effect on variation.
